one_liner: Pure-Rust port of GMP/FLINT integer algorithms; beats GMP (via rug) on sub-64-bit values and string parsing, not on large operands.
what_it_does: Malachite provides Natural and Integer (malachite-nz), Rational (malachite-q) and an in-progress arbitrary-precision Float (malachite-float) for Rust, with operator overloading plus a large trait library (DivRound, ModPow, gcd, roots, factorial, CRT, Kronecker symbol and more). Its algorithms are line-by-line ports of GMP 6.2.1 and FLINT routines in safe Rust. It has no C ABI, so it does not replace GMP in C or C++ code; inside Rust, the malachite-bigint crate offers a num-bigint-compatible drop-in.
how_it_is_fast: A Natural is an enum of Small(Limb) or Large(Vec<Limb>), so any value below 2^64 lives inline without a heap allocation, which is where it beats rug/mpz. For large operands it ports GMP's machinery: schoolbook, Toom-22/33/44/6h/8h and unbalanced Toom variants with GMP-style tuned thresholds (Toom-22 from 16 limbs on 64-bit), a small-prime FFT derived from Daniel Schultz's FLINT code plus Schonhage-Strassen from William Hart's FLINT code, GMP's divide-and-conquer and mu division with Newton inversion, and a subquadratic half-GCD. By-value operator overloads reuse the operand's buffer to avoid allocations in chains like &x + &y + &z.
when_to_use: Rust code dominated by values under 64 bits that must not overflow (interpreters, exact counters, property-test shrinkers): 10-bit add 2.1 ns vs rug 17.7 ns, gcd 8.5 ns vs 20.9 ns, pow 5.1 ns vs 41.6 ns
Parsing many decimal or hex strings: from_dec and from_hex beat rug at every size up to 10^4 bits (from_dec 8.37 us vs 11.51 us at 10^4 bits)
Pure-Rust, no_std or wasm targets that need GMP-class asymptotics (Toom, FFT, half-GCD) without a C toolchain or GMP build
Projects that want rationals and big integers with the same API family, or a num-bigint replacement via malachite-bigint (as RustPython does)
when_not_to_use: Operands above about 1,000 bits where raw speed matters: rug/GMP is faster on mul (8.28 us vs 4.52 us at 10^4 bits), div, pow and modular pow (250.90 ms vs 143.02 ms at 10^4 bits), and on every task in tczajka's suite (e to 10M digits 3.689 s vs 2.788 s)
Values of 65-128 bits: they already allocate (ubig_add at 100 bits 18.7 ns vs dashu 3.7 ns), so dashu is faster there
C or C++ codebases: there is no C API; call GMP directly

Closed-source distribution without accepting LGPL-3.0-only terms; Rust links crates statically by default, so the LGPL relinking obligations apply (issue #52 asked for a permissive license; it remains LGPL-3.0-only)
Arbitrary-precision floats in production: the README says malachite-float is not yet feature-complete

integration.form: crate (use the malachite meta-crate; malachite-nz holds the integer code)
integration.dependencies: malachite-base, itertools, libm, wide; optional serde, pyo3 (enable_pyo3), rand-based 'random' feature
integration.platforms: any Rust target; 64-bit limbs by default, 32_bit_limbs feature for u32 limbs; no_std supported (closed issue #97 reported std leaking in through wide under no-default-features)
integration.thread_safety: not documented explicitly; the crate is forbid(unsafe_code) unless enable_pyo3 is on, so Natural/Integer are ordinary owned values whose Send/Sync follow Rust's auto-trait rules
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: malachite-bigint is a drop-in for Rust's num-bigint; there is no rug- or GMP-compatible API (issue #91 'Rug API compatibility?' is open)

gotchas: Fast versions move quickly (0.9.1 in February 2026 to 0.12.0 in September 2026, minor-version bumps with API changes, e.g. issue #58 export incompatibility in 0.4.19+); pin versions

Issue #90 reported e to 1M digits at about 7000 ms on 0.7.0 and newer vs 800 ms on 0.6.1; it was closed 2026-06-18, the day before 0.9.2, so the benchmarked 0.9.1 may carry that regression (fix version not documented)
Past panics on valid inputs, all closed: extended_gcd 'mid > len' (#73), Natural::factorial assertion (#86), squaring 2^(2^25) (#55)
Mixed operations with primitives are deliberately not implemented (no Natural + u64); convert with Natural::from, which is cheap below 2^64
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick malachite over ibig and dashu when operands grow past a few thousand bits or you need gcd, modular and rational arithmetic with GMP-derived algorithms (the report finds it usually second to rug at 1,000-10^4 bits); pick dashu instead for 65-128-bit values or a permissive license, and FLINT or GMP itself from C/C++.
verified_claims_summary: In DRMacIver's public Criterion suite (rustc 1.92.0, Cargo default bench profile, Apple M2 Max), malachite-nz 0.9.1 beat rug 1.30.0 (GMP) on 10-bit operations (add, mul, gcd, extended gcd, pow, to_dec) and on hex/decimal parsing at all sizes up to 10^4 bits, but rug won add, sub, mul, div, pow and modular arithmetic from about 100-1,000 bits upward. The small-value wins come from avoiding rug's per-result heap allocation rather than from faster limb kernels.
status_note: Very active (commits to 2026-09-30, 0.12.0 released 2026-09-20, about 2.8 million recent crates.io downloads for malachite-nz) and copyable as LGPL-3.0-only safe Rust; floats are still incomplete.
